discovery: Spectroscopic imaging of the electronic structure of high-temperature superconductors in momentum and real space: d-wave gap, pseudogap and electronic order

nominees.name: Zhi-Xun Shen
nominees.affiliation: Stanford University and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, USA

nominees.name: J. C. Séamus Davis
nominees.affiliation: University of Oxford, UK and University College Cork, Ireland

subfield: Condensed matter physics (spectroscopy of quantum materials)
motivation: Shen and Campuzano turned angle-resolved photoemission into a precision probe of the single-particle spectral function. They directly established the anisotropic d-wave superconducting gap in the cuprates, discovered the normal-state pseudogap and its Fermi arcs, and revealed quasiparticle dispersion kinks that show strong electron-boson coupling. Davis invented spectroscopic-imaging scanning tunnelling microscopy. It images electronic states with atomic resolution, phase-sensitive quasiparticle interference that maps the gap in momentum space, and intra-unit-cell broken-symmetry and density-wave order. Together, these complementary momentum-space and real-space probes created new ways of seeing correlated electrons. They settled the pairing symmetry of high-Tc superconductivity and put the pseudogap and intertwined orders at the centre of quantum-materials physics. Their techniques are now standard worldwide, including for topological materials, heavy fermions, iron pnictides and moiré systems. This is the kind of instrumental advance that shapes an entire field.
